svg.title: Transponder and ADS-B Out areas
svg.desc: Side view of where a VFR airplane needs a Mode C transponder and ADS-B Out. Required in Class A, B and C, in the Mode C veil within 30 nautical miles of a Class B primary airport from the surface to 10,000 feet MSL, above the ceiling of Class B or C up to 10,000 feet MSL, and at and above 10,000 feet MSL over the 48 contiguous states and D.C., except at and below 2,500 feet AGL. ADS-B Out also applies over the Gulf of Mexico at and above 3,000 feet MSL within 12 nautical miles of the coast. Schematic, not to scale.
svg.text: Where a transponder and ADS-B Out are required (VFR)
Schematic side view, not to scale. Mode C (91.215) and ADS-B Out (91.225) cover nearly the same airspace.
At and above 10,000 ft MSL over the 48 states and D.C.
required, except at and below 2,500 ft AGL (so over high terrain the lowest 2,500 ft AGL is excluded)
Mode C veil: within 30 NM of the primary Class B airport, surface to 10,000 ft MSL
above Class B or C, within their lateral limits, up to 10,000 ft MSL: required
Outside the veil, below 10,000 ft MSL and outside Class A, B and C: no transponder is required.
Class A (18,000 ft MSL to FL 600): required. ADS-B Out also over the Gulf of Mexico,
at and above 3,000 ft MSL within 12 NM of the coast. Few exceptions, e.g. no engine-driven electrical system.
